overview: This bill renews federal funding authority for the Healthy Start Initiative, a long-running federal program under the Public Health Service Act that supports local efforts to reduce infant deaths and improve the health of mothers and babies. It authorizes $145 million a year for fiscal years 2026 through 2030 (federal budget years run October through September). "Authorizes" means it sets the amount Congress may provide; the actual money still has to be approved in yearly spending bills. The bill makes no other changes to how the program works. It was approved by the House Energy and Commerce Committee and placed on the House Union Calendar on October 3, 2025.
for: Supporters say a stable five-year authorization lets community programs that help mothers and infants plan ahead, supporting efforts to lower infant deaths in areas that need it most.
against: Critics say renewing the program at a set funding level without changes misses a chance to review whether it is working and to add accountability measures.
